description: Static identity map for every project the Supervisor is aware of. Work items, decisions, and conflicts reference projects only by the 'id' field below — never by inferring identity from file paths alone.

projects.notes: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no bundler.

projects.role: Learner workspace — independent learning, Concept Repository, legacy mission engine.
projects.deploy: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/firebase-hosting-merge.yml on merge to main; firebase-hosting-pull-request.yml for PR previews) — same pattern as ClassMate, separate workflow files, separate Firebase project.
projects.notes: Client-only, no build step, no Cloud Functions/backend today. Firestore rules committed but per the rules file's own top-of-file comment, not confirmed live on the production project as of last inspection (2026-09-13).

projects.role: Not a repository. Used to tag work items, decisions, and conflicts that concern the boundary between the two products rather than either codebase alone.
projects.notes: No shared repo, no shared Firebase project, no shared deploy pipeline exists or is proposed. Any 'cross-project' work item must still ultimately land as a change in exactly one of the two repos above (or a genuinely new, separate integration service, per open Decision 1 in decisions-log.md).

relationship_notes: ClassMate and Learning Hub are separate Git repositories, separate Firebase projects, and separate deploy pipelines. There is no code sharing, no shared Firestore project, and no build-time coupling of any kind today.

The only live coupling (as of the 2026-09 joint architecture research in learning-hub/docs/) is one-directional and static: ClassMate fetches Learning Hub's catalogue.json/packs.json directly, and can deep-link into Learning Hub via '?entry=<type>:<id>' URL params. Nothing pushes data from Learning Hub back to ClassMate.

A full, code-grounded integration contract already exists — see cross-project/dependencies.md, which indexes learning-hub/docs/CLASSMATE_LEARNING_HUB_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md, ..._DECISIONS.md, ..._RECOMMENDATIONS.md, and LEARNING_HUB_ARCHITECTURE_CURRENT_STATE.md rather than duplicating them.

Those four documents are currently UNTRACKED (not committed) in the learning-hub repo. The Supervisor must treat them as live, uncommitted work product — not yet a stable reference — until the user commits them.
